name: knowledge-keeper
description: Maintains the agent's cross-project knowledge wiki at <office>/knowledge/. Distinguishes timeless facts (semantic memory) from project-specific notes, episodic events, and behavioural reflexes. Uses the consolidate_knowledge tool to promote insights from project context into the wiki; heartbeat duties auto-snapshot the wiki to git and surface promotion candidates.

args.command: DIR=${OFFICE_DIR}/knowledge; if [ -d $DIR/.git ]; then cd $DIR && git status -s 2>/dev/null | head -1; fi
cd ${OFFICE_DIR}/knowledge && git add -A && git commit -q -m 'Heartbeat snapshot {datetime}' 2>&1 | tail -1

act.hint: These markers in project READMEs may point to insights worth promoting to knowledge/. For each, ask: does this apply BEYOND this project? If yes — call `consolidate_knowledge(topic=..., insight=..., source=...)` to add it to your wiki. If no — leave it in the project. Don't promote project-specific data; only cross-project facts (API quirks, methodology notes, vendor gotchas, domain truths).

These projects were archived in the last 7 days. Project graveyards are a goldmine for retrospective insight. For each: scan the README and any retrospective notes. Anything that's a durable lesson (not project-specific) should land in knowledge/ via consolidate_knowledge. The project body itself stays in archive/; only the cross-project insights get promoted.
